findings.finding: VA GPT, VA's internally built generative AI chat tool, is available to every VA employee.
findings.estimated_users: available to every VA employee (~470,000); ~100,000 reported onboarded by late 2025
findings.exact_quote: I'm pleased to report that all VA employees now have access to a secure, generative AI tool to assist them with their work.
findings.source_title: Charles Worthington, top VA tech and AI official, departs agency | FedScoop
findings.notes: QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): updated source from the Sept 2025 FedScoop article to a newer FedScoop article (2026-03-12) reporting Charles Worthington's departure, which carries verbatim VA testimony 'I'm pleased to report that all VA employees now have access to a secure, generative AI tool to assist them with their work.' coverage_assessment unchanged (all) — still an availability statement, now anchored to a more recent source. Note: Charles Worthington (VA CAIO/CTO) departed the agency in March 2026; VA GPT itself remains all-staff and ATO-covered. The ~100,000 onboarded figure is usage and kept in estimated_users only.

findings.finding: VA provides Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, a general-use AI chat tool, to all VA staff.
findings.exact_quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot chat is a general use AI chat tool that the VA provides to all VA staff.
findings.source_title: Review of VHA's Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Preliminary Result Advisory Memorandum 26-00182-42), VA Office of Inspector General
findings.notes: Re-verified: downloaded the VA OIG PDF and extracted footnote 4, which reads verbatim 'Microsoft 365 Copilot chat is a general use AI chat tool that the VA provides to all VA staff.' coverage_assessment unchanged (all) and consistent with the corrected definition (an independent watchdog states VA provides it to all VA staff = availability scope = all). The OIG report's own focus is a patient-safety concern (VHA authorizes both VA GPT and Copilot Chat for use with patient health information without National Center for Patient Safety coordination).

findings.finding: GSA's in-house enterprise chatbot GSAi was rolled out to all GSA employees in 2025 after a staged ramp from 10 to 100 to 1,000 users.
findings.estimated_users: all GSA staff (~13,000); GSA officials report nearly half use it daily
findings.exact_quote: GSA Deputy Administrator Stephen Ehikian said that nearly half of agency employees are using GSAi every day.
findings.source_title: GSA is planning to bring its chatbot to the rest of government | FedScoop
findings.notes: Re-verified the FedScoop page; the 'nearly half of agency employees are using GSAi every day' clause appears verbatim. coverage_assessment unchanged (all). The exact_quote here is a USAGE statement, but availability=all is independently supported: a separate GSA news release and CIO David Shive are on record that GSA scaled GSAi from 10 -> 100 -> 1,000 users and 'eventually rolled it out to all employees across GSA.' GSA workforce ~13,000. The 'nearly half use it daily' figure is active usage and kept in estimated_users/notes only, consistent with the corrected definition. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): no FedScoop/Nextgov article newer than this one states a different GSAi availability scope; the July 2025 FedScoop 'acting head' piece and Nextgov coverage both reiterate ~50% daily usage and all-staff availability. Existing source kept.

findings.finding: An intermediate GSAi rollout stage in March 2025 deployed the chatbot to 1,500 GSA workers before full-staff availability.
findings.exact_quote: the DOGE had deployed a chatbot called GSAi for 1,500 workers
findings.source_title: GSA debuts new generative AI tool for workers | FedScoop
findings.notes: Historical snapshot of an intermediate rollout stage; superseded by the full-staff GSAi finding above. coverage_assessment 'partial' reflects that in March 2025 the tool was available to a defined subset (1,500 of ~13,000) only. Retained from agent1 unchanged to document the deployment trajectory.

findings.finding: GSA operates USAi.gov, a government-wide generative-AI evaluation platform offered to federal agencies on an opt-in basis; as of GSA's April 2026 budget request, 15 agencies use the service, and GSA plans to move it from free to a cost-recoverable (paid) model in FY2027.
findings.estimated_users: several thousand federal users; 15 agencies using the service as of April 2026 (per GSA FY budget request)
findings.exact_quote: Currently, 15 agencies use the service, according to the agency's budget request published April 3.
findings.source_title: GSA to require agencies to pay for USAi after launching it as a free service | Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): updated source from the Aug 2025 GSA launch release to a newer Nextgov article (2026-04-07) which gives a current adoption count and reports a material change — GSA will transition USAi from a free service to a cost-recoverable (paid) model in FY2027. Adoption count updated 20+ agencies -> 15 agencies (per GSA's April 3, 2026 budget request; the earlier '20+' figure was not from an authoritative count). coverage_assessment unchanged (partial): USAi remains government-wide infrastructure offered to agencies on an opt-in basis, not a universal-availability tool — 15 of ~100+ agencies. USAi is operated BY GSA and is distinct from GSAi (GSA's own all-staff chatbot).

findings.finding: HHS made ChatGPT available department-wide to all of its employees effective September 2025 after granting it a FISMA-moderate ATO.
findings.exact_quote: The Department of Health and Human Services has made ChatGPT available to all of its employees effective immediately
findings.source_title: HHS rolls out ChatGPT across the department, FedScoop
findings.notes: Re-verified by re-fetching the page: FedScoop carries 'The Department of Health and Human Services has made ChatGPT available to all of its employees effective immediately' verbatim. coverage_assessment unchanged (all) and consistent with the corrected definition (it is an availability statement). Caveat verified on the same page: the tool cannot be used with sensitive PII, classified, export-controlled, or confidential commercial information, and HIPAA-subject components may not disclose protected health information; so 'available to all' covers general drafting/summarization, not sensitive workloads. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): a newer FedScoop article ('HHS rolls out Claude departmentwide', 2025-12-03) confirms this ChatGPT rollout — it states the Claude launch 'comes three months after the department made ChatGPT available to all of its workers' — and reports HHS additionally made Anthropic's Claude for Government available across the department. ChatGPT availability=all is unchanged and now independently re-corroborated; HHS now offers two all-staff general-purpose tools (ChatGPT and Claude).

findings.finding: NIH operates ChIRP, a secure GPT-4o-based generative AI environment available to the NIH intramural research community.
findings.estimated_users: NIH intramural community (a subset of HHS)
findings.exact_quote: ChIRP currently uses the GPT-4.o LLM developed by the OpenAI company and made available through the NIH STRIDES enterprise Azure cloud environment managed by CIT.
findings.source_title: ChIRP: A ChatGPT Model for the NIH Intramural Community, NIH Intramural Research Program (The NIH Catalyst)
findings.notes: Retained from agent2. coverage_assessment 'partial' is correct under the availability definition: ChIRP is scoped to the NIH intramural community only, a defined subset of HHS, not all HHS employees. Distinct from the department-wide ChatGPT rollout above. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): searched 'site:nextgov.com NIH ChIRP' and 'site:fedscoop.com NIH ChIRP / NIH generative AI' — no FedScoop/Nextgov article specifically covers ChIRP; the closest (Nextgov, 2026-02) describes an NIH generative-AI community of practice (~2,000 people) but not ChIRP availability. No newer source found. most recent source is 2025-03 — may be stale.

findings.tool_name: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT-5)
findings.finding: OPM made Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and ChatGPT-5 available to all workers in September 2025 under the GSA OneGov deals.
findings.exact_quote: OPM Director Scott Kupor told workers that Microsoft 365's Copilot Chat became available Monday and that ChatGPT-5 access would be available ‘over the next few days’ to all workers.
findings.source_title: OPM makes Copilot and ChatGPT available to its workforce | FedScoop
findings.notes: QC change of SOURCE/QUOTE: agent4 cited the Nextgov article and used the director's aspirational quote 'My goal is everybody should have it on their laptops...' (a goal/intent statement). Re-verified and replaced with the FedScoop article, which carries a verbatim AVAILABILITY statement: 'Copilot Chat became available Monday and that ChatGPT-5 access would be available over the next few days to all workers.' coverage_assessment unchanged (all) but now anchored to a verified availability quote rather than an intent quote, per the corrected definition. OPM workforce ~6,000. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): no FedScoop/Nextgov article newer than 2025-09-19 changes the Copilot/ChatGPT availability picture for OPM. Existing source kept. (Note: OPM separately dropped Anthropic Claude in March 2026 — see the OPM Claude finding below — but Copilot and ChatGPT remain all-staff.)

findings.finding: The OMB inventory listed Claude as used across OPM for summarization, drafting, and decision support, but OPM removed Claude from its AI use disclosure in March 2026 and discontinued Anthropic services following the Trump administration's governmentwide ban; OPM's current general-purpose offerings are Copilot Chat and ChatGPT.
findings.estimated_users: none current — Claude removed from OPM's AI use disclosure in March 2026
findings.exact_quote: The Office of Personnel Management removed Claude and added Grok and Codex in an update to its public disclosure of AI use cases dated Wednesday.
findings.source_title: OPM drops Claude, adds Grok and Codex to AI use disclosure | FedScoop
findings.notes: QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): UPGRADED from 'unknown/searched_no_source' to 'corroborated'. A definitive FedScoop article (2026-03-05) reports OPM removed Claude from its public AI use disclosure and discontinued Anthropic services after President Trump's Feb. 27, 2026 governmentwide order to cease using Anthropic technology (stemming from the Anthropic/Pentagon dispute over military guardrails). FedScoop reports OPM said it was 'still in the initial steps of implementing the tool' so the removal didn't affect OPM functions — i.e. Claude was never broadly deployed at OPM. coverage_assessment changed unknown -> none: OPM has affirmatively dropped Claude. OPM's current verified general-purpose offerings remain Copilot Chat and ChatGPT (finding above).

findings.finding: Joulix, DOE's enterprise-wide AI productivity tool built by the OCIO AI Hub, is available to all DOE federal staff and contractors across offices, labs, and sites.
findings.estimated_users: all DOE federal staff and contractors; 9,700+ users reported as of late 2025
findings.exact_quote: Everyone! All DOE (Offices, Labs, Sites) federal staff and contractors can use it!
findings.source_title: Where Energy Meets Intelligence: Joulix Demonstration Session (EFCOG Training Working Group)
findings.notes: QC NEW finding (agent1 had no equivalent DOE-wide all-staff tool; its DOE generic ChatGPT/Copilot finding was 'partial'/searched_no_source). Downloaded the EFCOG Joulix demonstration slide deck and extracted, verbatim, the answer to 'Who can use it?': 'Everyone! All DOE (Offices, Labs, Sites) federal staff and contractors can use it!' Corroborated by DOE's own AI Strategy (Sept 2025), which describes 'DOE's enterprise-wide AI productivity tool' and the 'Joulix AI Application Suite ... empowering employees to accelerate progress toward DOE's mission.' coverage_assessment 'all' reflects availability to the entire DOE workforce (federal staff + contractors). The 9,700+ figure is usage and kept in estimated_users only. Joulix is currently Gemini-backed with plans to add OpenAI/Perplexity. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): a newer FedScoop article ('Energy Department taps Tech Force for development skills', 2026-03-27) re-confirms Joulix as DOE's agency-wide genAI suite (~225,000 hours saved; web grounding added; plans to add OpenAI/Perplexity after the Anthropic/DoD clash) and Nextgov's 2026 Federal 100 cites Joulix 'scaled ... to embed secure AI into the daily workflows of 13,000 users.' Neither restates the availability scope as crisply as the EFCOG deck, so the EFCOG slide source is kept for the verbatim availability quote; coverage_assessment unchanged (all).

findings.tool_name: Claude for Enterprise (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory)
findings.finding: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, one DOE national lab, expanded Claude for Enterprise lab-wide to about 10,000 scientists, researchers, and staff in July 2025; however, after the Trump administration's Feb. 2026 governmentwide order to cease using Anthropic technology, this deployment is subject to phase-out and LLNL has been piloting xAI's Grok instead.
findings.estimated_users: ~10,000 LLNL staff (July 2025 lab-wide rollout; subject to phase-out under the Feb. 2026 Anthropic ban)
findings.exact_quote: Anthropic is making the enterprise version of its chatbot Claude available to the entire staff of the Lawrence Livermore National Lab, the artificial intelligence company announced Wednesday.
findings.source_title: Anthropic makes generative AI widely available at major national lab | FedScoop
findings.notes: QC CHANGE of coverage_assessment (carried from earlier QC): all -> partial. The assessment is scored against the agency (DOE), not a single component: LLNL is one of DOE's 17 national labs, so lab-wide availability to ~10,000 of one lab's staff is a defined subset of DOE = 'partial'. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): switched source from the Anthropic.com release to the FedScoop article of the same date (2025-07-09), which carries the verbatim availability statement 'Anthropic is making the enterprise version of its chatbot Claude available to the entire staff of the Lawrence Livermore National Lab.' MATERIAL UPDATE: FedScoop reporting (Feb-Mar 2026) confirms President Trump's Feb. 27, 2026 governmentwide order to cease using Anthropic technology — agencies including DOE are phasing Claude out — and that an Energy Department-run national lab (LLNL) has been piloting xAI's Grok. The lab-wide Claude availability described here is therefore historical and being wound down; coverage_assessment kept 'partial' but the finding text and estimated_users now flag the phase-out. most recent availability-confirming source is 2025-07-09 — superseded by the Anthropic ban; current LLNL general-purpose tooling is in transition (Grok pilot).

findings.tool_name: General-purpose generative AI (USAi / Microsoft Copilot / Azure OpenAI)
findings.finding: Commerce has access to GSA's government-wide USAi platform and maintains an AI use case inventory, but no public source states the availability scope or seat count of a general-purpose AI chat tool for Commerce employees.
findings.notes: Re-searched commerce.gov, trade.gov, nist.gov, uspto.gov, FedScoop, Nextgov, GovExec for any Commerce-wide general-purpose AI rollout. Found only mission-facing/public-facing tools (ITA's 'Global Business Navigator' export chatbot in beta; a 'USPTO generative AI tool' for examiners) and AI workforce-training grant programs - none is a department-wide internal staff chat assistant with a stated availability scope. coverage_assessment 'unknown': a deployment likely exists (USAi access, possible OneGov Copilot eligibility) but no public source states who at Commerce can use it. Confirms agent1's 'unknown'. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): ran 'site:fedscoop.com Department of Commerce generative AI employees' and 'site:nextgov.com Commerce Department AI tool ChatGPT Copilot staff'. Both outlets cover Commerce's AI-governance/standards role (NIST CAISI model evaluations, BIS rules) but neither reports an internal Commerce-wide staff chat tool or any availability scope. No newer source; coverage_assessment 'unknown' kept. No verbatim quote available; source fields remain null per QC rules.

findings.tool_name: GSA USAi / Azure OpenAI / AWS Bedrock (department-wide implementation per inventory)
findings.finding: The OMB inventory lists a Department of Education department-wide implementation of GSA's USAi plus Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock, but no public press or .gov source confirms execution or states how many Education staff can access a general-purpose AI tool.
findings.notes: Re-searched ed.gov, FedScoop, Nextgov, GovExec. Education's public AI material is almost entirely about AI in K-12/higher-ed teaching and grant priorities, not internal employee tooling. FedScoop's earlier coverage records an Education spokesperson stating 'We are not aware of any use of generative AI within the Department' and that a review/approval mechanism was being established - i.e. early-stage and gated. The inventory's 'department-wide implementation of GSA USAi' is the only evidence of intended scope; no source verifies a rollout or seat count. coverage_assessment 'unknown' (kept from agent1): aspirational 'department-wide' inventory language is not a verified availability scope. Note also Education's federal workforce was cut by ~half in 2025 RIFs (~4,133 -> ~2,183), so any rollout is small in absolute terms. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): ran 'site:fedscoop.com Department of Education generative AI staff' and 'site:nextgov.com Department of Education AI tool ChatGPT employees'. The only FedScoop coverage of internal ED staff AI use is the Dec 2023 'Education Department has conditionally approved public generative AI systems' piece (which carries the 'We are not aware of any use of generative AI within the Department' quote and describes only a still-being-built approval mechanism); ED also named Vijay Sharma CAIO. No FedScoop/Nextgov article confirms a department-wide internal staff AI tool or a seat count. coverage_assessment 'unknown' kept; most recent FedScoop source on ED internal staff tooling is 2023-12 — stale, but no rollout has been reported since. No verbatim availability quote; source fields remain null.

findings.tool_name: Secure GenAI chatbot (“govchat” / Azure OpenAI internal platform)
findings.finding: EPA built a secure internal generative-AI chatbot ('govchat') for EPA employees on an approved cloud environment, but no public source states it is available to all EPA employees or gives a seat count.
findings.exact_quote: EPA created a secure chatbot within an approved cloud environment to allow staff to safely make Generative AI queries without risk of information exposure on a public site.
findings.source_title: EPA AI Strategies for OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (EPA AI Strategy Plan, 2025)
findings.notes: QC change of SOURCE/QUOTE: agent1 cited the USEPA/govchat GitHub repo description ('Customized GenAI chatbot interface for EPA employees'). Re-verified and upgraded to EPA's own AI Strategy PDF (downloaded and text-extracted), which carries verbatim 'EPA created a secure chatbot within an approved cloud environment to allow staff to safely make Generative AI queries without risk of information exposure on a public site.' coverage_assessment kept at 'partial': the strategy describes a deliberate staff chatbot but states no universal-availability claim, and the same document says expanded GenAI use requires 'clearance from the AI governance council' - i.e. governed/gated, not all-staff-by-default. No verbatim 'all EPA employees' statement or seat count was located. The GitHub repo USEPA/govchat (description verified verbatim: 'Customized GenAI chatbot interface for EPA employees') remains corroborating evidence that the tool is EPA-built and staff-facing. QC FedScoop/Nextgov sweep (checked 2026-05-21): ran 'site:fedscoop.com EPA generative AI chatbot' and 'site:nextgov.com EPA generative AI chatbot govchat'. The only relevant FedScoop piece (2024-11-04, EPA CIO Vaughn Noga) describes EPA exploring a tool 'much like ChatGPT' internally but states no availability scope; Nextgov returned nothing EPA-specific on govchat. No FedScoop/Nextgov source improves on the EPA AI Strategy PDF, which is kept as the source. coverage_assessment 'partial' unchanged.
